ai-at-work.title: Signal’s Meredith Whittaker wants you to remember that AI chatbots ‘are not your friends’
ai-at-work.excerpt: "These are not your friends. These are not conscious beings. These are not sentient interlocutors.”
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Signal's president Meredith Whittaker is reminding people that AI chatbots are statistical prediction machines, not thinking entities with your best interests in mind. This matters because workplace adoption of AI tools is exploding, and if employees anthropomorphize these systems, they'll make poor decisions about what information to share and how much to trust the recommendations. After thirty years watching technology hype cycles, I'll say this: the companies selling you AI friendship bracelets are counting on you forgetting this basic fact, so bookmark her comments for when your boss insists the chatbot "just gets it."

ai-at-work.title: AI, user data and the asymmetry of understanding
ai-at-work.excerpt: Every time users belatedly discover that an artificial intelligence feature has been drawing on their data in ways they did not fully grasp, the reaction is often an instinctive sense of violation – o
ai-at-work.dwp_take: SiliconAngle reports that companies keep getting caught using employee data for AI training without clear consent, sparking privacy violations and trust breakdowns. This matters because digital workplace leaders are literally the ones deploying these tools to their workforce, which means they're sitting between angry employees and vendors who buried the data practices in terms nobody reads. The real problem isn't the AI, it's that we still haven't figured out how to have honest conversations about what we're trading away, and pretending everyone understands the fine print won't make it true.

ai-at-work.title: Agentic AI’s challenge is getting agents to act like a team, not a crowd
ai-at-work.excerpt: Adding more artificial intelligence agents to the workflow doesn’t make an enterprise smarter. In fact, it can make operations harder to manage. The problem is not the capabilities of individual agent
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Companies are discovering that throwing multiple AI agents at a problem doesn't automatically make things better, and coordinating them is actually harder than building them in the first place. This matters because digital workplace leaders are about to spend a lot of money on agent-based AI systems, and if those agents can't play nice together, you've just built an expensive mess that's harder to manage than the manual process you replaced. After three decades in this space, I can tell you this is just the same coordination problem we've been wrestling with since the first enterprise software integration, except now the things that won't talk to each other are hallucinating.

ai-at-work.title: Elastic reportedly acquires site reliability engineering startup Deductive AI
ai-at-work.excerpt: Elastic NV has reportedly acquired Deductive AI Inc., a startup with a platform that helps enterprises fix errors in their technology infrastructure. TechCrunch on Thursday cited a source as saying th
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Elastic picked up Deductive AI for up to $85 million, roughly doubling the startup's previous valuation, to add AI-powered error detection and fixing capabilities to their infrastructure monitoring platform. This matters because SRE teams are drowning in alerts and manual troubleshooting, so automation that actually catches problems before they cascade is genuinely useful. Elastic is basically admitting their existing tools need AI smarts or they'll get left behind, which is fair, though let's see if the integration doesn't just create another bloated feature nobody uses.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft broke some OLE automations with latest Windows update
tools-tech.excerpt: Microsoft Office users may find that some of their applications are failing to open when called on by third-party applications. It’s an issue that has emerged after the latest round of Microsoft updat
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft's latest Windows update broke OLE automation connections, which means Office apps like Word and Excel won't launch properly when called from third-party software like Zotero or dental practice management tools. This matters because most enterprises have workflows built on these automation bridges, so users suddenly can't access critical documents from their specialized business apps. After three decades watching Microsoft updates, I can tell you this is the kind of "surprise" that makes IT teams love their jobs even less than they already do.

tools-tech.title: OpenAI adds spend controls and usage analytics to ChatGPT Enterprise
tools-tech.excerpt: OpenAI has introduced spend controls and enhanced usage analytics for ChatGPT Enterprise to enable organizations to monitor AI adoption, track consumption across teams, and set budgets for AI usage. B
tools-tech.dwp_take: OpenAI just added budget controls and usage dashboards to ChatGPT Enterprise so companies can finally see who's burning through their AI tokens and set spending limits across teams. For digital workplace leaders, this is the table stakes stuff you need if you're going to deploy AI tools responsibly and explain to your CFO why you're spending money on this thing. The catch that made me laugh: you can now watch your money disappear in real time and know exactly which department is responsible, but you still won't know if any of it actually matters to your bottom line.

tools-tech.title: Q&A: Temporal aims to be the reliability backbone for an agentic AI economy
tools-tech.excerpt: As AI shifts from output-generating large language models (LLMs) to armies of agents taking actions on their own, there is a growing threat that failures could affect system reliability. Temporal, a B
tools-tech.dwp_take: Temporal is pitching itself as the reliability safety net for autonomous AI agents that operate independently rather than just generating text. This matters because digital workplaces are about to deploy these agents into production systems, and when they fail (not if), you need something that can pick up exactly where things broke without losing data or creating chaos. I'd believe it when I see it, but honestly, someone needs to solve the "my AI agent went rogue and deleted the wrong folder" problem before we all start relying on these things.

tools-tech.title: How to bring the best Android 17 features to any Android phone today
tools-tech.excerpt: Google’s latest and greatest Android version is officially now out in the world and available — but if you’re using any phone other than a Pixel, that doesn’t mean much for you just yet. The reason wh
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google released Android 17 this week, but most non-Pixel phones won't get it anytime soon because manufacturers have to customize and roll out updates on their own schedules. This matters to digital workplace pros because your organization's mobile device fleet will be fragmented across OS versions for months, creating security patches headaches and support complexity. After three decades watching this cycle repeat, I can tell you that "latest and greatest" means precisely nothing to 90 percent of users until their phone maker decides it does, which is why IT teams should stop waiting and start planning for extended heterogeneity.

digital-culture.title: More fathers are becoming the primary caregiver
digital-culture.excerpt: Al said goodbye to his daughters every night before he drove to work. He’d hand off childcare to his wife when she returned home from work and start his commute during dinnertime. Al, a Connecticut-ba
digital-culture.dwp_take: More fathers are taking on primary caregiving responsibilities while their partners work traditional schedules, forcing creative arrangements like night shifts to make it all work. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to stop assuming the traditional nuclear family still exists and build flexibility into every policy, tool, and meeting time. The fact that Al needed to work nights just to be present for his kids shouldn't require a pseudonym in 2024, and it's a wake-up call that our workplace cultures haven't actually caught up to real life.

digital-culture.title: 5 counterintuitive tips for working more effectively
digital-culture.excerpt: Below, Melissa Swift shares five key insights from her new book, Effective: How to Do Great Work in a Fast-Changing World. [Photo: Wiley] Melissa is the founder and CEO of the consulting firm Anthrome
digital-culture.dwp_take: Melissa Swift, a veteran consultant with stints at every major consulting firm, published five counterintuitive tips for effective work in a fast-changing world. Digital workplace leaders need to understand these insights because most teams are still operating on outdated productivity assumptions that actively hurt performance. Here's the thing though: if you need a consultant to tell you the obvious isn't working, you've probably been ignoring your own people's feedback for way too long.

industry-news.title: Ditch the Cloud: 5 Best Self-Hosted Photo Video-Gallery Options
industry-news.excerpt: Looking to store your media privately? Explore five top self-hosted photo and video gallery solutions for full control and customization. The post Ditch the Cloud: 5 Best Self-Hosted Photo Video-Galle
industry-news.dwp_take: TechRepublic rounded up five self-hosted alternatives to cloud-based photo and video storage, giving organizations options to keep their media completely on premises with full control over data. For digital workplace teams dealing with sensitive content, compliance requirements, or just philosophically opposed to vendor lock-in, knowing what self-hosted tools actually work matters a lot. Here's the thing though: self-hosted sounds great until someone has to patch the server at midnight, so make sure you've got the IT bandwidth before you ditch the cloud entirely.

industry-news.title: Apple Patches Beats Studio Buds Flaw That Could Enable Wiretapping
industry-news.excerpt: Apple patched a Beats Studio Buds Bluetooth flaw that could let nearby attackers listen through the microphone during pairing. The post Apple Patches Beats Studio Buds Flaw That Could Enable Wiretappi
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple fixed a Bluetooth vulnerability in Beats Studio Buds that allowed attackers within range to eavesdrop through the microphone during the pairing process. This matters because plenty of knowledge workers use these buds for calls and video meetings, meaning sensitive conversations could have been intercepted by someone nearby. The real kicker is that this flaw existed during the most vulnerable moment, pairing, when people are least thinking about security and most focused on just getting the darn things to connect.

industry-news.title: Apple to Work With Intel on US Chip Production, Trump Says
industry-news.excerpt: Trump says Apple will work with Intel on US chip production, a potential foundry win that could shift Apple’s supply chain options and US chip strategy. The post Apple to Work With Intel on US Chip Pr
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple and Intel are apparently teaming up on US chip manufacturing, according to Trump's announcement, which could reshape where and how Apple sources its processors. For digital workplace folks, this matters because supply chain stability directly impacts everything from hardware refresh cycles to device availability for your workforce. Honestly, I'll believe this partnership sticks when I see chips actually rolling off US production lines, because tech executives say a lot of things that sound good until quarterly earnings show up.

industry-news.title: Microsoft Project vs Smartsheet: Best Choice for 2026
industry-news.excerpt: Is Microsoft Project similar to Smartsheet? Use our guide to compare the main differences in features and pricing between Microsoft Project and Smartsheet. The post Microsoft Project vs Smartsheet: Be
industry-news.dwp_take: TechRepublic published a comparison guide between Microsoft Project and Smartsheet to help people choose between the two project management tools. Digital workplace pros need to understand these distinctions because picking the wrong tool wastes budget, fragments workflows, and confuses teams who are already drowning in too many apps. Honestly, the real answer is usually "whatever your enterprise already uses," but I appreciate TechRepublic trying to inject some rationality into a decision that's more often made in a budget meeting than based on actual feature needs.
